title: A different kind of continuum limit for the three-dimensional U(1) gauge theory
authors: Andreas Athenodorou, Claudio Bonati, Ivan Soler Calero
abstract: In three-dimensional compact U(1) lattice gauge theory color confinement can be understood analytically through the dynamics of magnetic monopoles. However, its continuum limit is pathological, since the ratio of the glueball masses to the square root of the string tension vanishes as the continuum limit is approached. We investigate a simple extension of the Wilson action in which the total number of lattice monopoles is coupled to an additional parameter $μ$. By tuning $β$ and $μ$ simultaneously, we identify a line of constant physics along which the ratio of the lightest glueball mass to the square root of the string tension remains constant. We further show that the same scaling is satisfied, within numerical uncertainties, by the other low-lying glueball masses considered in this work. Along this trajectory, the string tension in lattice units decreases with increasing $β$, thus suggesting that the modified lattice action may provide a regularization of three-dimensional compact U(1) gauge theory with a physically well-behaved continuum limit.
summary: This paper addresses the pathological continuum limit of 3D U(1) lattice gauge theory by modifying the standard action to include a term dependent on lattice monopoles. By tuning two parameters ($ eta$ and $\mu$) along a specific trajectory, the authors demonstrate that a physically meaningful constant ratio between glueball mass and string tension can be maintained. This suggests a viable regularization scheme for the theory.
main_problem: The continuum limit of the three-dimensional compact U(1) lattice gauge theory is pathological because the ratio of glueball masses to the square root of the string tension vanishes.
main_result: By modifying the lattice action to couple to the total number of lattice monopoles, the authors found a line of constant physics where this ratio remains constant, suggesting a physically well-behaved continuum limit.
method: The authors modified the Wilson action by adding a term proportional to the monopole number and tuned two parameters ($ eta$ and $\mu$) simultaneously to trace this line of constant physics.
model_or_system: The system is the three-dimensional compact U(1) lattice gauge theory. The model is the standard Wilson action extended by a term coupling to the total number of lattice monopoles, $S = - eta \sum 	ext{Re} P - \mu N_m$.
key_observables: Glueball masses ($m_0$), string tension ($\sqrt{\sigma}$), and the ratio $m_0/\sqrt{\sigma}$.
important_parameters: Lattice coupling $ eta$, monopole coupling $\mu$, and the continuum limit ($ eta 	o \infty$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the dilute monopole gas approximation, although the results suggest this approximation might be circumvented by the bounded nature of lattice monopole charges.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the pathology of the standard continuum limit. It then introduces the modified action and demonstrates that tuning $ eta$ and $\mu$ along a specific trajectory keeps the ratio $m_0/\sqrt{\sigma}$ constant, suggesting a regularization.
why_interesting: While focused on gauge theory, the concept of finding a 'line of constant physics' by tuning parameters to regularize a pathological limit is a general concept in critical phenomena and phase transitions relevant to statistical mechanics.
